risks.note: All approved formulations are made by contract manufacturers on loan licence or principal-to-principal basis. Output, quality and delivery therefore sit outside the Company's own control, and management's growth plan is explicitly to fix this by entering a long-term MOU for a dedicated FDA/WHO-approved facility near Mumbai and Ahmedabad - i.e. the dependency is acknowledged as the constraint to be solved.
risks.risk: Dependence on third-party contract manufacturers - the Company owns no plant

risks.note: The MD&A states the industry is highly regulated with stringent, restrictive quality norms, that products must be registered after testing for safety, efficacy and environmental impact, and that regulations differ from country to country. Some customers do business with the Company only on the basis of it being the approved source of supply, so loss or lapse of an approval directly removes the right to serve those customers.
risks.risk: Regulatory approval and registration dependency in a highly regulated industry

risks.note: The Opportunities list describes vaccines and certain formulations as under approval with huge market demand, and the phased vaccine launch (Hep A, IPV first; Pneumococcal and Varicella within 3-4 years) is the core of the stated business plan. The revenue from this plan is contingent on approvals that had not been received at the reporting date.
risks.risk: Vaccines and certain formulations are still 'under approval' - the growth plan is pre-approval

risks.note: The Company reports that its business activities comprise one business segment - Pharmaceutical Formulations and API Products - so there is no diversification within the reported structure to absorb a shock to pharma formulations or API pricing. The Company also has no subsidiary, joint venture or holding company.

Management lists fluctuations in raw material prices and increases in input cost that can cause upward pricing among its threats, and the cautionary statement names raw material prices and selling prices as the assumptions it cannot guarantee. In a business whose cost base is dominated by materials used and consumed, unrecovered input inflation compresses an already thin margin.
risks.risk: Raw material price and input cost inflation with limited pass-through

risks.note: The threats list flags too many players entering and exiting the market and the Opportunities and Threats section flags competition from new players within the country, which pressures both pricing and the Company's ability to hold distributor and hospital relationships built on its own brand.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity - too many players entering and exiting the market

risks.note: Changes in government policies head the threats list, and the cautionary statement names governing and applicable laws and political factors among the assumptions underlying management's outlook. The vaccine plan is itself premised on Government Health Incentive Programmes, so policy withdrawal cuts both ways.
risks.risk: Government policy change and pharmaceutical pricing / regulatory policy risk

risks.note: The Opportunities and Threats section states that global trade wars can pose a challenge to international trade impacting the company, while the growth plan depends on expanding the sales footprint in export markets and on imported / indented APIs and intermediates.
risks.risk: Export and international trade exposure to global trade wars
